# Medical assistant app

The original React chatbot retains its layout and styling. **View conversation
history** opens a matching panel with a clickable graph, invocation timeline, and
**Ledger & tasks** view. All activity is generated by actual runs; there are no
sample conversations or seeded task lists.

## Run locally

Use Python 3.11+ and Node.js. In two terminals, from this repository:

```powershell
cd app/backend
python -m venv .venv
.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pip install -r requirements.txt
.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m uvicorn main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --reload --reload-exclude '.venv/*'
```

If Python is available through the Windows launcher, use `py -3.12 -m venv .venv`.
The virtual environment has already been created in this worktree.

```powershell
cd app/frontend
npm ci
npm run dev -- --host 127.0.0.1
```

Open <http://127.0.0.1:3000>. Vite proxies `/api` to port 8000.
API documentation: <http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs>.

To let the backend load a configuration file from a different checkout, without
copying its contents, use this launcher from the repository root:

```powershell
./app/start-backend.ps1 -EnvFile 'C:\path\to\app\backend\.env'
```

It passes only the file path via `MEDICAL_ASSISTANT_ENV_FILE` and uses the requested
`gpt-5.4-nano` deployment (override with `-ModelDeployment` when needed). The backend
reads the file itself. Environment variables take precedence over file values.
`GET /api/deployments` is a read-only local setup check for deployment names.

## Foundry configuration and agent names

Copy `backend/.env.example` to `backend/.env`. Supply your existing Foundry project
endpoint and model deployment name. Authenticate with a credential supported by
`DefaultAzureCredential`, such as your Azure CLI login. Restart the backend after
changing `.env`. Without configuration, the app opens normally and live requests
return an actionable 503; no traces are fabricated.

On the first live request, the backend looks up these agents in that project and
creates a prompt-agent version for each missing name:

| Workflow role | Foundry agent name |
| --- | --- |
| Coordinator / manager | `medical-assistant-manager` |
| Web researcher (web search) | `medical-assistant-researcher` |
| WHO knowledge specialist (preconfigured WHO KB) | `medical-assistant-who-knowledge` (version `2`) |
| Formatter | `medical-assistant-communicator` |
| Safety reviewer | `medical-assistant-safety-reviewer` |

The WHO specialist uses the existing `medical-assistant-who-knowledge` agent version `2`,
including its Foundry knowledge-base configuration. The backend verifies that
this exact agent version exists and does not create or replace it.
The web researcher uses Foundry's web search tool. Agent text deltas appear in the
conversation history panel as each response streams.

Look for these names under **Agents** in the configured Foundry project. Registration
requires permission to create agent versions. Matching existing agents are reused. If an agent registered by this app has a
different model or instructions, a new version is created, preserving old versions.
Unowned mismatched definitions are rejected. Versions are resolved once per backend
lifetime; restart to pick up changes. The panel's **Agent names in
Foundry** section shows the registered names and versions actually used. A pending
label means registration has not yet been verified, not that a remote agent exists.

`clients/foundry_team.py` owns registration and version resolution. Instructions live
in `agents/definitions.py`. This follows the notebook's registered `FoundryAgent` +
`MagenticBuilder` architecture with stable names, rather than generating new names
for every request. The notebook's framework versions and round/stall/reset limits
are preserved.

## Actual ledgers, tasks, and traces

`agents/orchestration.py` observes the standard Magentic manager without replacing
its planning behavior. It emits the actual task ledger (facts and plan), replans,
and progress ledger fields: request satisfaction, loop detection, progress, next
speaker, and the instruction sent to that speaker. Task rows come from these real
assignments. Their queued/running/completed/failed states follow the corresponding
agent invocation; tasks are not inferred from a predefined routine.

Agent middleware records each invocation's input context, text response, duration,
and status. Planning and progress-ledger calls count separately, as do repeated
specialist calls. Graph edges summarize coordinator-specialist exchanges; selecting
an edge shows the relevant calls and shared context. This is an application-level
trace, not an import of Azure Monitor spans or hidden model reasoning.

The API streams call-start, call-finish, ledger, task, and agent-identity events while
the workflow runs. A final reply completes the stream. Responses arrive per call,
not token by token. A stopped/disconnected request cancels the local workflow;
provider-side work already accepted can still incur usage. Runs time out after 300
seconds (`ORCHESTRATION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`). A fresh workflow isolates each request.
Prior chat turns are quoted in one initial task, as required by Magentic.

`POST /api/chat` keeps the compatible `reply` field and adds `calls`.
`POST /api/chat/stream` returns newline-delimited JSON; blank lines are heartbeats.
Inputs are limited to 8,000 characters per message, 40 prior messages, and 80,000
characters of combined context.

The app keeps traces/history in browser memory only, cleared on refresh or **Clear
conversation**. It does not log message contents. Foundry service-side retention
follows your project configuration. This local workshop demo has no authentication
layer; use synthetic data.

## Verify

```powershell
cd app/backend
.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

Tests execute the actual Magentic workflow with a deterministic test model, without
Azure, to verify call counts, context, real ledger events, task lifecycle, streaming,
and error handling. Azure registration is tested with a mocked project client.

```powershell
cd app/frontend
npm run build
```

UI references were reviewed at <https://21st.dev/community/components/s/ai-chat>.
The original app styles are retained; no new UI dependencies were added.
